content: 1. Risk of Bias: There were no significant concerns regarding bias in the studies. The 2015 study was assessed as having a moderate risk of bias. Mannequins were treated as if they were human participants in the quality assessment. However, there was a lack of detailed reporting for several domains of the ROBINS-I tool, including outcome measurement. Additionally, there was no blinding of outcome assessors, though the simulated nature of the study reduced the likelihood of bias in the outcomes. 2. Inconsistency: There were no serious issues with inconsistency across the studies. 3. Indirectness: The evidence was considered to have very serious indirectness. This was due to the reliance on simulation studies and the use of non-human participants, as well as differences in the evaluated personal protective equipment (PPE) beyond just the presence or absence of head and neck coverings. 4. Imprecision: The evidence was rated as having serious imprecision. This was attributed to the small number of participants and the failure to meet the optimal information size (OIS) threshold. 5. Publication Bias: There were no significant concerns regarding publication bias. 6. Outcome Measurements: Time to Reach Critical Core Temperature (39°C): The studies compared various conditions (e.g., E4 vs. E2, E3 vs. E2, E4 vs. E1) and found that the time to reach a critical core temperature was generally lower (worse) in some conditions. The certainty of evidence was very low due to serious imprecision and the small sample size (6 participants in 1 study). Body Surface Skin Temperature: Measurements at the time of reaching a critical core temperature showed higher skin temperatures in certain conditions (e.g., E4 vs. E2, E3 vs. E2). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious imprecision. Heat Sensation: Heat sensation at the time of reaching a critical core temperature was higher in some conditions (e.g., E4 vs. E2, E3 vs. E2). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious imprecision. Core Temperature After 80 Minutes of Activity: Core temperatures were higher in certain conditions (e.g., B-E4 vs. E2, B-E3 vs. E2). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious imprecision. Skin Temperature After 80 Minutes of Activity: Skin temperatures were higher in some conditions (e.g., B-E4 vs. E2, B-E3 vs. E2). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious imprecision. Heat Sensation After 80 Minutes of Activity: Heat sensation was higher in certain conditions (e.g., B-E4 vs. E2, B-E3 vs. E2). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious imprecision. Discomfort After 80 Minutes of Activity: Discomfort levels were higher in some conditions (e.g., B-E4 vs. E2, B-E3 vs. E2). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious imprecision. Core Temperature at the End of Exercise: Core temperatures were higher in certain conditions (e.g., E3 vs. E1, E2 vs. E1). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious risk of bias and imprecision. Skin Temperature at the End of Exercise: Skin temperatures were higher in some conditions (e.g., E3 vs. E1, E2 vs. E1). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious risk of bias and imprecision. Heart Rate at the End of Exercise: Heart rates were higher in certain conditions (e.g., E3 vs. E1, E2 vs. E1). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious risk of bias and imprecision. Sweat Weight Loss per Hour: Sweat weight loss was higher in some conditions (e.g., E3 vs. E1, E2 vs. E1). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious risk of bias and imprecision. Heat Sensation at the End of Exercise: Heat sensation was higher in certain conditions (e.g., E3 vs. E1, E2 vs. E1). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious risk of bias and imprecision. Thermal Comfort at the End of Exercise: Thermal comfort was higher in some conditions (e.g., E3 vs. E1, E2 vs. E1). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious risk of bias and imprecision. Perceived Exertion at the End of Exercise: Perceived exertion was higher in certain conditions (e.g., E3 vs. E1, E2 vs. E1). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious risk of bias and imprecision. Breathing Comfort at the End of Exercise: Breathing comfort was higher in some conditions (e.g., E3 vs. E1, E2 vs. E1). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious risk of bias and imprecision. Wetness at the End of Exercise: Wetness levels were higher in certain conditions (e.g., E3 vs. E1, E2 vs. E1). The evidence was rated as very low due to serious risk of bias and imprecision. 7. General Observations: The studies were conducted under simulated conditions, which limits the generalizability of the findings to real-world scenarios. The use of mannequins and the lack of human participants further reduce the applicability of the results. The small sample sizes and lack of blinding in outcome assessments also contribute to the low certainty of the evidence. This detailed interpretation highlights the limitations and findings of the studies, emphasizing the need for caution when interpreting the results due to the very low certainty of evidence.
